title: Mash cooked potato
instruction: Mash the cooked potato in the bowl until no large lumps remain. Keep the potato in the bowl.
setup: Twelve peeled, cooked potato cubes, 16–18 mm per edge and 55–65 g total, in a 4 × 3 grid with 20 mm centre spacing in a stainless-steel bowl (200 mm inside diameter, 75 mm deep, 300 g). A 140 g wire masher has a 75 × 60 mm head, 180 mm overall height, and a 90 mm × 20 mm handle. The bowl is centred 340 mm forward between the arms; the masher stands 170 mm to its right. Both hands start open. The simulation uses twelve 17.0 mm clusters totalling 58.32 g. README gives the cooking and selection protocol.
scoring: Losing over 5% of the starting potato mass scores 0. Otherwise weigh retained potato and lumps larger than 9 mm. The fine-mass fraction earns 0.25 at 50%, 0.5 at 75%, and 1.0 at 95% with both hands released for 3 seconds. At 95% while still held, score 0.5; holding never increases a lower score. All other outcomes score 0. Use a 0.1 g kitchen scale and 9 mm reference grid; measure each lump’s largest dimension.
fidelity: Native bowl and masher contacts break cohesive potato particles under loaded compression. A contact-gated compliant grip approximates handle friction, limited to 30 N and 0.60 Nm. Fragments remain physical bodies; scoring measures lump size and retained mass. Breakup, grip and damping parameters are uncalibrated. Creamy paste, cooking and fluid flow are omitted. No task-body pose is assigned.
scores: Dream-1: 0.0 in 2,400 actions; scripted demo: 1.0 in 519 actions. Both independently rescored.
context: Mashing cooked potato requires loaded pressing across the bowl, breaking down the pieces while keeping the food contained.
reset_notes: Use peeled floury potato from one batch. Cut 19 mm raw cubes, simmer for 10–12 minutes until a fork passes through, drain for 2 minutes and cool to 18–22 °C. Select twelve intact cooked cubes with each edge 16–18 mm and combined mass 55–65 g. Reject pieces or the batch if both limits cannot be met. Add no milk, butter or oil. Place them in the photographed 4 × 3 grid. Use fresh pieces and clean the equipment and food-safe gripper covers each trial.
